summary: A mobile- and laptop-friendly storefront for buying mobile internet bundles, with automated payment, purchase, and fulfillment. The service depends on external network/reseller and payment APIs, so end-to-end automation must be validated against the providers selected during requirements review.

workspaceSignals.decisionReason: The workspace contains only a README and no existing application manifests, services, or Azure configuration.

questions.question: Which programming language for Bundle Storefront?
questions.rationale: The workspace has no existing frontend stack; TypeScript is a strong default for a responsive commerce experience.

questions.question: Which frontend framework for Bundle Storefront?
questions.rationale: React + Vite is a broadly supported choice for a mobile- and laptop-friendly storefront.

questions.question: Describe the storefront experience: bundle discovery and comparison, country/operator selection, mobile and laptop priorities, guest versus signed-in checkout, account identity, purchase status and delivery confirmation, receipts, and how users should see cancellations or refunds.
questions.recommendedChoice: Responsive bundle catalog and checkout with clear purchase, delivery, and refund status.
questions.answer: Falaaa is a responsive Ghanaian data marketplace for MTN, Telecel, and AirtelTigo (AT). The customer experience includes bundle discovery, network selection, recipient phone entry, checkout, transaction history, and delivery/refund status. The private business dashboard manages orders, customers, agents, suppliers, wholesale balances, pricing, margins, transactions, and reports. The first release supports customers and agents; use phone-based OTP identity and retain low-friction checkout. Design for Android phones, iPhones, tablets, and laptops with responsive layouts.
questions.rationale: The user specified bundle sales, mobile and laptop use, and asked to clarify account identity and delivery confirmation.

questions.question: Which programming language for Purchase API?
questions.rationale: No backend language is present in the workspace; TypeScript is a practical default for API integrations.

questions.question: Which framework or hosting model for Purchase API?

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Managed serverless HTTP API and provider webhooks

options.label: Azure Container Apps
options.description: Managed container hosting for an API service

questions.rationale: A managed API host can receive checkout and provider callbacks; hosting preference and API constraints need confirmation.

questions.question: Describe the purchase API requirements. Include launch country/market and mobile networks/operators; how bundle inventory, pricing, and purchase APIs or reseller-aggregator access will be supplied (including sandbox, credentials, contract, and API limitations); accepted payment methods and preferred payment provider; currency, markup/commission, fees/taxes, refund and chargeback rules; account identity and delivery confirmation; expected average and peak orders/traffic; launch timing, hosting/region preferences, and any compliance or support constraints.
questions.recommendedChoice: Integrate approved bundle and payment providers, expose checkout and status APIs, and persist auditable order and payment state.
questions.answer: Ghana launch with MTN, Telecel, and AirtelTigo (AT). Supplier API/reseller access and licensed payment API access are available; exact provider names, API capabilities, credentials, sandbox results, and commercial contracts must be verified before launch. Accept supported mobile money methods through the payment gateway; never collect or store wallet PINs. Use GHS, configurable retail/agent prices and commissions, and show supplier/payment costs separately for margin reporting. The customer pays before fulfillment is submitted; only confirm success after supplier delivery confirmation. Support pending, failed, cancelled, refunded, and disputed states with automated reconciliation and refunds where provider rules permit. The initial release supports retail customers and agents, with role-based access and agent limits. Expected volume, launch date, exact fee/tax rules, refund/chargeback policy, audit retention, and hosting region remain to be confirmed; use provider-independent integrations and a configurable, scalable hosting design.
questions.rationale: These market, provider, payment, commercial, identity, volume, and launch decisions were not specified and need user input.

questions.question: Which programming language for Fulfillment Worker?
questions.rationale: No existing worker stack is present; TypeScript allows sharing types with the API if desired.

questions.question: Which hosting model for Fulfillment Worker?

options.label: App Service background task
options.description: Background processing hosted alongside an app

questions.rationale: Queue-driven processing supports unattended fulfillment and retryable work; the provider integration and hosting preference may change this choice.

questions.question: Describe the fulfillment automation and operations you expect: when to submit a bundle purchase relative to payment authorization/capture; provider idempotency and safe retry behavior; delivery polling or callback/webhook confirmation; timeout and duplicate handling; order/payment reconciliation cadence and source of truth; failure, cancellation, refund, and chargeback paths; audit-log retention; alerts, customer support, and cases that require escalation instead of silent/manual intervention. Note any provider API constraints or peak-volume expectations.
questions.recommendedChoice: Automated queue-based fulfillment with idempotent submissions, bounded retries, delivery confirmation, reconciliation, auditable state transitions, and alert-driven exception handling.
questions.answer: Use an Azure Functions queue-triggered fulfillment worker for automated provider submission, bounded retries, delivery polling/webhook confirmation, duplicate and timeout handling, reconciliation, and alerts. Payment must be verified before dispatch; use idempotency keys and never silently retry ambiguous non-idempotent supplier operations. Automate refunds only when payment and supplier state establish eligibility; alert operations/support for unresolved exceptions, without making routine purchases dependent on human intervention. Persist auditable order/payment state and protect credentials in a managed secret store. Provider-specific retry, callback, and refund behavior must be validated against the available APIs.
questions.rationale: The user requires automated purchase and fulfillment and explicitly requested these reliability, security, and support controls.

questions.question: Which data stores does your app need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The app does not persist data or use storage, queues, or caches

questions.rationale: Order, payment, bundle, reconciliation, and audit state need durable relational storage; background fulfillment needs a queue; Blob Storage is also required by the recommended Azure Functions hosting model.

questions.question: Does this app need user login?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Add a user sign-in flow and authenticated API access

options.label: No
options.description: No user sign-in or authenticated API access

questions.answer: Yes. Use phone-based OTP authentication for customers and agents, with role-based administrator access. The customer storefront and private business dashboard are responsive web experiences; no native mobile app is required for the initial release.
questions.rationale: The user asked to clarify account identity; confirm whether purchases require customer accounts or may use guest checkout.
